title: 3D Dot Game Heroes
subtitle: An old adventure with visible depth

body: 3D Dot Game Heroes is Silicon Studio's PlayStation 3 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 5 November 2009. The kingdom of Dotnia faces a returning evil, sending a hero through fields and dungeons in search of the means to stop it. The structure recalls early console adventures, but the landscape and characters are built from small three-dimensional blocks. Those visible cubes make an old visual language into a physical-looking world. Monsters scatter into pieces, while water and lighting give the deliberately simple shapes an unexpectedly elaborate presentation.

When the hero's health is full, swinging the sword produces a blade of extraordinary size. Keeping that advantage changes the value of avoiding even a small hit. Sword improvements can extend its length and width, letting the player shape how much of a room one attack can reach. Other equipment includes familiar adventure tools such as a boomerang, bow and lantern. Progress comes from exploring the map, finding objects and using them to solve the obstacles inside a dungeon before facing its main threat.

A character editor lets the player assemble a hero from the same blocks that define the world. It can produce a conventional adventurer or a more unlikely figure, making the nostalgic journey visibly personal. References and jokes acknowledge the games whose structure it borrows, while the block-based presentation supplies its own identity. FromSoftware published the original Japanese release, with Atlus and SouthPeak handling later regions. Reviewers generally welcomed its affectionate approach to early action adventures and the contrast between familiar rules and the more modern treatment of their shapes.
